title.zh: 卷九十九 志第五十二 禮二
title.raw: 卷九十九 志第五十二 禮二 Volume 99 Treatises 52: Rites 2

sentences.zh: 南郊壇制。

translations.literal: Regulations for the Southern Suburban Altar.
translations.idiomatic: The System of the Southern Suburban Altar.

sentences.zh: 梁及後唐郊壇皆在洛陽。

translations.literal: The suburban altars of Liang and Later Tang were all in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under both the Liang and Later Tang, the suburban altars were located in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 宋初始作壇于東都南薰門外，四成、十二陛、三壝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, an altar was first built outside the Nanxun Gate of the Eastern Capital, with four tiers, twelve stairways, and three enclosures.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song dynasty was first established, an altar was erected outside the Nanxun Gate of the Eastern Capital, with four tiers, twelve stairways, and three ritual enclosures.

sentences.zh: 設燎壇於內壇之外丙地，高一丈二尺。

translations.literal: A fire altar was set up at the bing position outside the inner altar, twelve feet in height.
translations.idiomatic: A fire altar was installed at the bing compass point beyond the inner altar, rising twelve feet high.

sentences.zh: 設皇帝更衣大次於東壝東門之內道北，南向。

translations.literal: The emperor's great dressing tent was set up north of the inner road at the east gate of the eastern enclosure, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's great dressing pavilion was placed north of the inner pathway at the east gate of the eastern enclosure, oriented to the south.

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖六年，始築外壝，周以短垣，置靈星門。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tiansheng under Renzong, the outer enclosure was first built, surrounded by a low wall, and the Lingxing Gate was installed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Tiansheng era (1028), Emperor Renzong had the outer enclosure built for the first time, ringed with a low perimeter wall, and the Lingxing Gate was added.

sentences.zh: 親郊則立表於青城，表三壝。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally performed suburban sacrifice, markers were erected at the Green City, marking the three enclosures.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor performed the suburban rites in person, boundary markers were set up at the Green City to delineate the three enclosures.

sentences.zh: 神宗熙寧七年，詔中書、門下參定青城殿宇門名。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xining under Shenzong, an edict ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery to deliberate and fix the names of halls and gates at the Green City.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Xining era (1074), Emperor Shenzong ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery to determine the names of the halls and gates at the Green City.

sentences.zh: 先是，每郊撰進，至是始定名，前門曰泰禋，東偏門曰迎禧，正東門曰祥曦，正西門曰景曜，後三門曰拱極，內東側門曰夤明，西側門曰肅成，殿曰端誠，殿前東、西門曰左右嘉德，便殿曰熙成，後園門曰寶華，著為定式。

translations.literal: Previously, at each suburban sacrifice newly composed names were submitted; only now were the names fixed — the front gate was called Taichong, the east side gate Yingxi, the main east gate Xiangxi, the main west gate Jingyao, the three rear gates Gongji, the inner east side gate Yinming, the west side gate Sucheng, the hall Duanqing, the east and west gates before the hall the Left and Right Jiade Gates, the side hall Xicheng, the rear garden gate Baohua — established as fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Until then, new names had been proposed with each suburban sacrifice; at this point they were fixed for good: the front gate Taichong, the east side gate Yingxi, the main east gate Xiangxi, the main west gate Jingyao, the three rear gates Gongji, the inner east side gate Yinming, the west side gate Sucheng, the main hall Duanqing, the east and west gates before the hall called the Left and Right Jiade Gates, the side hall Xicheng, the rear garden gate Baohua — all set as permanent standards.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年二月，詔內壝之外，眾星位周環，每二步植一杙，繚以青繩，以為限域。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Yuanfeng, an edict ordered that outside the inner enclosure, around the positions of the host of stars, a stake was to be planted every two paces, encircled with blue cord, to serve as a demarcated area.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Yuanfeng (1078), an edict directed that beyond the inner enclosure, stakes were to be set every two paces around the stellar positions, bound with blue cord to mark the boundary.

sentences.zh: 既而詳定奉祀禮文所言：「《周官》外祀皆有兆域，後世因之，稍增其制。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Detailed Regulations for Suburban Sacrifice Rites stated: "In the Offices of Zhou, outer sacrifices all had demarcated precincts; later ages followed this and gradually expanded the system.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, the Detailed Regulations for Suburban Sacrifice Rites observed: "In the Offices of Zhou, every outer sacrifice had a demarcated precinct; later dynasties followed this practice and gradually enlarged the regulations.

sentences.zh: 國朝郊壇率循唐舊，雖儀注具載圜丘三壝，每壝二十五步，而有司乃以青繩代內壝，誠不足以等神位、序祀事、嚴內外之限也。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's suburban altar largely followed Tang precedent; although the ritual manuals fully record the three enclosures of the Round Mound, each enclosure twenty-five paces, yet the responsible officials used blue cord in place of the inner enclosure — truly insufficient to rank the divine positions, order the sacrificial affairs, and enforce the distinction between inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's suburban altar largely followed Tang practice; although the ritual manuals fully describe the Round Mound's three enclosures of twenty-five paces each, the responsible officials had substituted blue cord for the inner enclosure — which was truly inadequate to rank the divine seats, order the sequence of rites, and enforce the distinction between inner and outer precincts.

sentences.zh: 伏請除去青繩，為三壝之制。

translations.literal: We respectfully request removing the blue cord and establishing the system of three enclosures.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully request that the blue cord be removed and the three-enclosure system be restored.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 徽宗政和三年，詔有司討論壇壝之制。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe under Huizong, an edict ordered the responsible officials to discuss the system of altar and enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Zhenghe era (1113), Emperor Huizong ordered the responsible offices to deliberate on the regulations governing the altar and its enclosures.

sentences.zh: 十月，禮制局言：「壇舊制四成，一成二十丈，再成十五丈，三成十丈，四成五丈，成高八尺一寸；

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the Bureau of Ritual Regulations stated: "The old altar system had four tiers — the first tier twenty zhang, the second fifteen zhang, the third ten zhang, the fourth five zhang, each tier eight feet one inch in height;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, the Bureau of Ritual Regulations reported: "Under the old altar system there were four tiers — the first twenty zhang wide, the second fifteen zhang, the third ten zhang, the fourth five zhang, each tier rising eight feet one inch;

sentences.zh: 十有二陛，陛十有二級；

translations.literal: there were twelve stairways, each stairway twelve steps;
translations.idiomatic: there were twelve stairways, each with twelve steps;

sentences.zh: 三壝，二十五步。

translations.literal: three enclosures, twenty-five paces each.
translations.idiomatic: and three enclosures of twenty-five paces each.

sentences.zh: 古所謂地上圜丘、澤中方丘，皆因地形之自然。

translations.literal: What antiquity called the round mound on high ground and the square mound in a marshland both followed the natural terrain.
translations.idiomatic: What antiquity called the round mound on elevated ground and the square mound in marshland both conformed to natural topography.

sentences.zh: 王者建國，或無自然之丘，則于郊澤吉土以兆壇位。

translations.literal: When a sovereign established his state, if there was no natural mound, then on auspicious ground at the suburban marsh he marked out the altar site.
translations.idiomatic: When a sovereign founded his state, if no natural mound was available, he selected auspicious ground at the suburban marsh to mark out the altar site.

sentences.zh: 為壇之制，當用陽數，今定為壇三成，一成用九九之數，廣八十一丈，再成用六九之數，廣五十四丈，三成用三九之數，廣二十七丈。

translations.literal: The system for constructing an altar should employ yang numbers; it is now fixed as three tiers — the first tier using the number nine-times-nine, breadth eighty-one zhang; the second using six-times-nine, breadth fifty-four zhang; the third using three-times-nine, breadth twenty-seven zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The construction of an altar should follow yang numerology; it is now fixed at three tiers — the first tier based on nine times nine, eighty-one zhang in breadth; the second on six times nine, fifty-four zhang; the third on three times nine, twenty-seven zhang.

sentences.zh: 每成高二十七尺，三成總二百七十有六，《乾》之策也。

translations.literal: Each tier twenty-seven feet in height; the three tiers total two hundred seventy-six — the tally of Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Each tier rises twenty-seven feet, the three tiers totaling two hundred seventy-six feet — the number associated with the hexagram Qian.

sentences.zh: 為三壝，壝三十六步，亦《乾》之策也。

translations.literal: For three enclosures, each enclosure thirty-six paces — also the tally of Qian.
translations.idiomatic: The three enclosures are each thirty-six paces wide — likewise derived from the number of Qian.

sentences.zh: 成與壝地之數也。

translations.literal: " These are the numbers for tiers and enclosures in area.
translations.idiomatic: " Such are the numerological measures for the tiers and enclosures.

sentences.zh: 」詔行之。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered this put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered these regulations implemented.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，高宗至揚州，庶事草創，築壇于州南門內江都縣之東南，詔東京所屬官吏奉祭器、大樂、儀仗、法物赴行在所。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan, Gaozong arrived at Yangzhou; all affairs were hastily improvised, and an altar was built southeast of Jiangdu County inside the south gate of the prefecture; an edict ordered officials subordinate to the Eastern Capital to convey sacrificial vessels, great music, ceremonial regalia, and ritual implements to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyan (1128), Emperor Gaozong reached Yangzhou; with everything still hastily improvised, an altar was erected southeast of Jiangdu County inside the prefecture's south gate, and an edict directed officials from the Eastern Capital to bring sacrificial vessels, court music, ceremonial regalia, and ritual implements to the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 紹興十三年，太常寺言：「國朝圓壇在國之東南，壇側建青城齋宮，以備郊宿。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shaoxing, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices stated: "Our dynasty's Round Mound is in the southeast of the realm; beside the altar the Green City fasting palace was built to provide for suburban lodging.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Shaoxing (1143), the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "Our dynasty's Round Mound stands in the southeast of the realm, with a Green City fasting palace built beside the altar to accommodate the emperor's overnight stay before the suburban rites.

sentences.zh: 今宜於臨安府行宮東南修建。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to build it southeast of the traveling palace in Lin'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It is now appropriate to construct one southeast of the traveling palace in Lin'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 」於是，遂詔臨安府及殿前司修建圓壇，第一成縱廣七丈，第二成縱廣一十二丈，第三成縱廣一十七丈，第四成縱廣二十二丈。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an edict ordered Lin'an Prefecture and the Palace Front Command to build the Round Mound — the first tier seven zhang in length and breadth, the second twelve zhang, the third seventeen zhang, the fourth twenty-two zhang.
translations.idiomatic: " Accordingly, an edict directed Lin'an Prefecture and the Palace Front Command to build the Round Mound: the first tier seven zhang square, the second twelve zhang, the third seventeen zhang, and the fourth twenty-two zhang.

sentences.zh: 一十二陛，每陛七十二級，每成一十二綴。

translations.literal: Twelve stairways, each stairway seventy-two steps, each tier twelve courses.
translations.idiomatic: There were twelve stairways, each with seventy-two steps and each tier built in twelve courses.

sentences.zh: 三壝，第一壝去壇二十五步，中壝去內壝、外壝去中壝各半之。

translations.literal: Three enclosures — the first enclosure twenty-five paces from the altar; the middle enclosure from the inner, and the outer from the middle, each half that distance.
translations.idiomatic: Three enclosures were laid out: the innermost twenty-five paces from the altar, with the middle and outer enclosures each placed at half that interval beyond the preceding one.

sentences.zh: 燎壇方一丈，高一丈二尺，開上南出戶，方六尺，三出陛，在壇南二十步丙地。

translations.literal: The fire altar was one zhang square, one zhang two feet high, with an opening above and a door facing south six feet square, three outward stairways, placed at the bing position twenty paces south of the altar.
translations.idiomatic: The fire altar measured one zhang square and one zhang two feet high, with an opening on top and a southern door six feet square, three outward stairways, situated at the bing compass point twenty paces south of the altar.

sentences.zh: 其青城及望祭殿與行事陪祠官宿齋幕次，並令絞縛，更不修蓋。

translations.literal: The Green City, the Hall of Gazing Sacrifice, and the fasting tent quarters for officiating and attendant sacrifice officials were all ordered lashed together and not to be roofed over.
translations.idiomatic: The Green City, the Hall of Gazing Sacrifice, and the fasting tent quarters for officiating and attendant officials were all to be lashed together as temporary structures, without permanent roofing.

sentences.zh: 先是，張杓為京尹，議築齋宮，可一勞永逸，宇文價曰：「陛下方經略河南，今築青城，是無中原也。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhang Biao was metropolitan magistrate, he proposed building a fasting palace that would settle the matter once and for all; Yuwen Jia said: "Your Majesty is just now planning recovery of the Central Plains — to build a Green City now is to abandon the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhang Biao served as metropolitan magistrate, he had proposed building a permanent fasting palace to settle the matter once and for all; Yuwen Jia objected: "Your Majesty is still planning the recovery of the Central Plains — to build a Green City now would be to concede that the heartland is lost.

sentences.zh: 」遂罷役。

translations.literal: " The work was then halted.
translations.idiomatic: " The construction was accordingly halted.

sentences.zh: 神位。

translations.literal: Divine Positions.
translations.idiomatic: Divine Seats.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年十一月，詳定郊廟奉祀禮文所言：「按東漢壇位，天神從祀者至千五百一十四，故外設重營，以為等限。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Yuanfeng, the Detailed Regulations for Suburban and Temple Sacrifice Rites stated: "According to Eastern Han altar positions, attendant worship of heavenly spirits reached one thousand five hundred fourteen; therefore outer layered encampments were set up to serve as ranked limits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first year of Yuanfeng (1078), the Detailed Regulations for Suburban and Temple Sacrifice Rites observed: "Under the Eastern Han altar arrangement, spirits attending the heavenly sacrifice numbered as many as 1,514; hence outer layered encampments were established to demarcate ranks.

sentences.zh: 日月在中營內南道，而北斗在北道之西，至於五星中宮宿之屬，則其位皆中營，二十八宿外宮星之屬，則其位皆外營。

translations.literal: The sun and moon were on the southern path within the middle encampment, while the Northern Dipper was west of the northern path; as for the Five Stars and inner-palace asterisms, their positions were all in the middle encampment; the outer-palace stars of the Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions had their positions all in the outer encampment.
translations.idiomatic: The sun and moon stood on the southern path within the middle encampment, while the Northern Dipper was placed west of the northern path; the Five Stars and inner-palace asterisms all occupied the middle encampment, and the outer-palace stars of the Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions the outer encampment.

sentences.zh: 然則為重營者，所以等神位也。

translations.literal: Thus layered encampments serve to rank divine positions.
translations.idiomatic: Layered encampments, then, served to rank the divine seats.

sentences.zh: 唐因隋制，設為三壝，天神列位不出內壝，而御位特設於壇下之東南。

translations.literal: Tang followed Sui practice, establishing three enclosures; heavenly spirits' ranked positions did not extend beyond the inner enclosure, while the imperial seat was specially set southeast below the altar.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang followed Sui practice with three enclosures: the heavenly spirits' seats did not extend beyond the inner enclosure, while the imperial seat was specially placed southeast below the altar.

sentences.zh: 若夫公卿分獻、文武從祀，與夫樂架饌幔，則皆在中壝之內，而大次之設乃在外壝。

translations.literal: As for the separate offerings of dukes and ministers, the attendant worship of civil and military officials, and the music stands and food curtains, all were within the middle enclosure, while the great tent was set in the outer enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: The separate offerings of dukes and ministers, the attendant worship of civil and military officials, and the music stands and food curtains all lay within the middle enclosure, while the great tent was placed in the outer enclosure.

sentences.zh: 然則為三壝者，所以序祀事也。」

translations.literal: Thus three enclosures serve to order sacrificial affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Three enclosures, then, served to order the sequence of sacrificial affairs."

sentences.zh: 景德三年，鹵簿使王欽若言：「漢以五帝為天神之佐，今在第一龕；

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde, the Imperial Escort Commissioner Wang Qinruo stated: "Han took the Five Emperors as assistants to the Heavenly Spirit; now they are in the first niche;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingde (1006), Imperial Escort Commissioner Wang Qinruo observed: "The Han regarded the Five Emperors as assistants to the Heavenly Spirit, yet they now occupy the first niche;

sentences.zh: 天皇大帝在第二龕，與六甲、嶽瀆之類接席；

translations.literal: the Great Heavenly Emperor is in the second niche, sharing mats with the Six Jia, mountains and rivers, and the like;
translations.idiomatic: the Great Heavenly Emperor is in the second niche, seated alongside the Six Jia, the sacred mountains and rivers, and similar spirits;

sentences.zh: 帝座，天市之尊，今與二十八宿、積薪、騰蛇、杵臼之類同在第三龕。

translations.literal: the Imperial Seat, lord of the Heavenly Market, now shares the third niche with the Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions, Piled Firewood, Soaring Serpent, Pestle and Mortar, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: the Imperial Seat, sovereign of the Heavenly Market, now shares the third niche with the Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions, Piled Firewood, Soaring Serpent, Pestle and Mortar, and similar minor stars.

sentences.zh: 卑主尊臣，甚未便也。

translations.literal: A lowly lord and exalted minister — most inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: To place the exalted below and the humble above is most improper.

sentences.zh: 若以北極、帝坐本非天帝，蓋是天帝所居，則北極在第二，帝坐在第三，亦高下未等。

translations.literal: If the Northern Pole and Imperial Seat are originally not the Heavenly Thearch but rather where the Heavenly Thearch dwells, then the Northern Pole in the second and Imperial Seat in the third is also unequal in rank.
translations.idiomatic: If the Northern Pole and Imperial Seat are not the Heavenly Thearch himself but merely his dwelling places, then placing the Northern Pole in the second niche and the Imperial Seat in the third is likewise a misordering of rank.

sentences.zh: 又太微之次少左右執法，子星之次少孫星，望令司天監參驗。

translations.literal: Furthermore, among the asterisms of Supreme Palace Enclosure the Left and Right Law-Enforcers are missing; among the asterisms of the Son Star, the Grandson Star is missing — it is hoped the Directorate of Astronomy will investigate and verify.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, the asterisms of the Supreme Palace Enclosure lack the Left and Right Law-Enforcers, and the Son Star asterisms lack the Grandson Star — we request that the Directorate of Astronomy investigate and verify.

sentences.zh: 」乃詔禮儀使、太常禮院、司天監檢定之。

translations.literal: " An edict then ordered the Commissioner of Rites, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Ritual Office, and the Directorate of Astronomy to examine and fix this.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict thereupon directed the Commissioner of Rites, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Ritual Office, and the Directorate of Astronomy to examine the matter and determine the correct arrangement.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使趙安仁言：「按《開寶通禮》，元氣廣大則稱昊天，據遠視之蒼然，則稱蒼天。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of Rites Zhao Anren stated: "According to the Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao, when primordial qi is vast and great it is called Vast Heaven; viewed from afar in its azure expanse, it is called Azure Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner of Rites Zhao Anren argued: "According to the Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao, when primordial qi is vast and great it is called Vast Heaven; viewed from afar in its azure expanse, it is called Azure Heaven.

sentences.zh: 人之所尊，莫過於帝，托之於天，故稱上帝。

translations.literal: What humans revere most is none other than the Thearch; entrusting this to Heaven, it is therefore called Supreme Thearch.
translations.idiomatic: What humans revere above all is the Thearch; entrusting this reverence to Heaven, it is therefore called the Supreme Thearch.

sentences.zh: 天皇大帝即北辰耀魄寶也，自是星中之尊。

translations.literal: The Great Heavenly Thearch is the Brilliant Treasure of the Northern Asterism — thus the most exalted among stars.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Heavenly Thearch is the Brilliant Treasure of the Northern Asterism — the most exalted among the stars.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：'日月麗乎天，百穀草木麗乎土。

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'The sun and moon are attached to Heaven; the hundred grains and grasses and trees are attached to Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "The sun and moon are attached to Heaven; the hundred grains, grasses, and trees are attached to Earth.

sentences.zh: '又曰：'在天成象，在地成形。

translations.literal: ' It also says: 'In Heaven forms are completed; on Earth shapes are formed.
translations.idiomatic: " It also says: "In Heaven forms are completed; on Earth shapes are formed.

sentences.zh: '蓋明辰象非天，草木非地，是則天以蒼昊為體，不入星辰之列。

translations.literal: ' This clarifies that stellar images are not Heaven and plants are not Earth — thus Heaven takes azure vastness as its substance and does not enter the ranks of stars.
translations.idiomatic: " This shows that stellar images are not Heaven itself and plants are not Earth itself — Heaven takes azure vastness as its substance and does not belong among the stars.

sentences.zh: 又《郊祀錄》：'壇第二等祀天皇大帝、北斗、天一、太一、紫微、五帝坐，差在行位前，餘內官諸位及五星、十二辰、河漢，都四十九坐齊列，俱在十二陛之間。

translations.literal: Furthermore, the Record of Suburban Sacrifice states: 'The second rank of the altar sacrifices to the Great Heavenly Thearch, Northern Dipper, Celestial One, Supreme One, Purple Subtlety, and Seats of the Five Thearchs, slightly before the procession positions; the remaining inner-palace positions together with the Five Stars, Twelve Chronograms, and River Han — forty-nine seats in all, aligned together, all between the twelve stairways.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Suburban Sacrifice also states: "The altar's second rank sacrifices to the Great Heavenly Thearch, the Northern Dipper, Celestial One, Supreme One, Purple Subtlety, and the Seats of the Five Thearchs, placed slightly ahead of the procession positions; the remaining inner-palace seats together with the Five Stars, Twelve Chronograms, and River Han — forty-nine seats in all, aligned between the twelve stairways.

sentences.zh: ' 唐建中間，司天冬官正郭獻之奏：'天皇、北極、天一、太一，准《天寶敕》併合升第一等。

translations.literal: ' During the Jianzhong period of Tang, Winter Official of the Directorate of Astronomy Guo Xianzhi memorialized: 'The Great Heavenly Thearch, Northern Pole, Celestial One, and Supreme One — pursuant to the Tianbao edict — should all be jointly elevated to the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: " During the Jianzhong period of Tang, Guo Xianzhi, Winter Official of the Directorate of Astronomy, memorialized that the Great Heavenly Thearch, Northern Pole, Celestial One, and Supreme One should all be jointly elevated to the first rank pursuant to the Tianbao edict.

sentences.zh: '貞元二年親郊，乙太常議，詔復從《開元禮》，仍為定制。

translations.literal: ' In the second year of Zhenyuan, when the emperor personally performed suburban sacrifice, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated on the day yi; an edict restored following the Kaiyuan Rites, and this remained the fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor personally performed suburban sacrifice in the second year of Zhenyuan (786), the Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated, and an edict restored the arrangement of the Kaiyuan Rites as the permanent standard.

sentences.zh: 《郊祀錄》又云：'壇第三等有中宮、天市垣、帝坐等十七坐，並在前。

translations.literal: The Record of Suburban Sacrifice also states: 'The third rank of the altar has the Central Palace, Heavenly Market Enclosure, Imperial Seat, and seventeen seats in all, all placed forward.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Suburban Sacrifice further states: "The altar's third rank includes the Central Palace, Heavenly Market Enclosure, Imperial Seat, and seventeen seats in all, all placed in the forward positions.

sentences.zh: '《開元禮義羅》云：'帝有五坐，一在紫微宮，一在大角，一在太微宮，一在心，一在天市垣。

translations.literal: ' The Exegesis of the Kaiyuan Rites states: 'The Thearch has five seats — one in the Purple Subtlety Palace, one at Great Horn, one in the Supreme Palace Enclosure, one at Heart, one in the Heavenly Market Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: " The Exegesis of the Kaiyuan Rites explains: "The Thearch has five seats — one in the Purple Subtlety Palace, one at Great Horn, one in the Supreme Palace Enclosure, one at Heart, and one in the Heavenly Market Enclosure.

sentences.zh: '即帝坐者非直指天帝也。

translations.literal: ' Thus the Imperial Seat does not directly refer to the Heavenly Thearch.
translations.idiomatic: " Thus the Imperial Seat does not refer directly to the Heavenly Thearch himself.

sentences.zh: 又得判司天監史序狀：'天皇大帝一星在紫微勾陳中，其神曰耀魄寶，即天皇是星，五帝乃天帝也。

translations.literal: Moreover, from the acting director of the Directorate of Astronomy Shi Xu's memorial: 'The single star of the Great Heavenly Thearch is within the Purple Subtlety Hooked Array; its spirit is called Brilliant Treasure — the Great Heavenly Thearch is this star; the Five Thearchs are the Heavenly Thearch.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, from the acting director of the Directorate of Astronomy Shi Xu's memorial: "The Great Heavenly Thearch is a single star within the Purple Subtlety Hooked Array; its spirit is called Brilliant Treasure — the Great Heavenly Thearch is this star, while the Five Thearchs represent the Heavenly Thearch.

sentences.zh: 北極五星在紫微垣內，居中一星曰北辰，第一主月為太子，第二主日為帝王，第三為庶子，第四為嫡子，第五為天子之樞，蓋北辰所主非一，又非帝坐之比。

translations.literal: The five stars of the Northern Pole are within the Purple Subtlety Enclosure; the central star is called Northern Asterism — the first governs the moon as heir apparent, the second governs the sun as sovereign, the third the secondary son, the fourth the legitimate son, the fifth the pivot of the Son of Heaven; thus what the Northern Asterism governs is not singular, and it is not comparable to the Imperial Seat.
translations.idiomatic: The five stars of the Northern Pole lie within the Purple Subtlety Enclosure; the central star is called the Northern Asterism — the first governs the moon as heir apparent, the second the sun as sovereign, the third the secondary son, the fourth the legitimate son, the fifth the pivot of the Son of Heaven; the Northern Asterism governs many things and is not comparable to the Imperial Seat.

sentences.zh: 太微垣十星有左右執法、上將、次將之名，不可備陳，故總名太微垣。

translations.literal: The ten stars of the Supreme Palace Enclosure bear the names Left and Right Law-Enforcer, Senior General, and Junior General — they cannot all be enumerated, and are therefore collectively named the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: The ten stars of the Supreme Palace Enclosure bear names such as Left and Right Law-Enforcer, Senior General, and Junior General — too numerous to list individually — and are therefore collectively called the Supreme Palace Enclosure.

sentences.zh: 《星經》舊載孫星，而《壇圖》止有子星，辨其尊卑，不可同位。

translations.literal: The Classic of Stars formerly recorded the Grandson Star, while the Altar Diagram has only the Son Star — distinguishing their ranks, they cannot share a position.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Stars records the Grandson Star, while the Altar Diagram lists only the Son Star — given their difference in rank, they cannot share the same position.

sentences.zh: '竊惟《壇圖》舊制，悉有明據，天神定位，難以躋升，望依《星經》，悉以舊禮為定。」

translations.literal: ' In our humble judgment the old regulations of the Altar Diagram all have clear warrant; the positioning of heavenly spirits is difficult to elevate — we hope to follow the Classic of Stars and fix everything according to the old rites."
translations.idiomatic: " In our humble judgment, the old Altar Diagram regulations all rest on clear authority; the positioning of heavenly spirits cannot readily be elevated — we request that everything be fixed according to the Classic of Stars and the established rites."

sentences.zh: 欽若復言：「舊史《天文志》並云：北極，北辰最尊者。

translations.literal: Qinruo again stated: "The Astronomical Treatises of the old histories all say: the Northern Pole — the Northern Asterism is the most exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo replied: "The Astronomical Treatises of the old histories all state that the Northern Pole — the Northern Asterism — is the most exalted.

sentences.zh: 又勾陳口中一星曰天皇大帝，鄭玄注《周禮》謂：'禮天者，冬至祭天皇於北極也。

translations.literal: Furthermore, within the mouth of the Hooked Array one star is called the Great Heavenly Thearch; Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Rites of Zhou states: 'Those who sacrifice to Heaven — at the winter solstice sacrifice to the Heavenly Thearch at the Northern Pole.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, one star within the mouth of the Hooked Array is called the Great Heavenly Thearch; Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Rites of Zhou states: "Those who sacrifice to Heaven offer sacrifice to the Heavenly Thearch at the Northern Pole at the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: '後魏孝文禋六宗，亦升天皇五帝上。

translations.literal: ' Emperor Xiaowen of Later Wei performed the li sacrifice to the Six Ancestors, also elevating the Heavenly Thearch above the Five Thearchs.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei performed the li sacrifice to the Six Ancestors, likewise elevating the Heavenly Thearch above the Five Thearchs.

sentences.zh: 按晉《天文志》：'帝坐光而潤，則天子吉，威令行。

translations.literal: According to the Jin Astronomical Treatise: 'When the Imperial Seat is bright and lustrous, the Son of Heaven is fortunate and his authority prevails.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Jin Astronomical Treatise: "When the Imperial Seat is bright and lustrous, the Son of Heaven is fortunate and his authority prevails.

sentences.zh: '既名帝坐，則為天子所占，列於下位，未見其可。

translations.literal: ' Since it is named Imperial Seat, it is what the Son of Heaven occupies — to place it in a lower rank is not seen as acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: " Since it is named the Imperial Seat, it is what the Son of Heaven occupies — to place it in a lower rank is hardly appropriate.

sentences.zh: 又安仁議，以子、孫二星不可同位。

translations.literal: Moreover, Anren argued that the Son and Grandson stars cannot share a position.
translations.idiomatic: Anren also argued that the Son and Grandson stars cannot share the same position.

sentences.zh: 陛下方洽高禖之慶，以廣維城之基，苟因前代闕文，便為得禮，實恐聖朝茂典，尤未適中。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is just now enjoying the blessings of the High Matchmaker to broaden the foundation of the fortified walls — if we simply follow lacunae in former ages' texts and call it proper ritual, we truly fear the flourishing regulations of the sage court are especially not well suited.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is now enjoying the blessings of the High Matchmaker to strengthen the imperial house — to treat lacunae in former ages' texts as sufficient warrant for proper ritual would, I fear, ill suit the flourishing regulations of our sage court.

sentences.zh: 」詔天皇、北極特升第一龕，又設孫星于子星位次，帝坐如故。

translations.literal: " An edict specially elevated the Great Heavenly Thearch and Northern Pole to the first niche, also established the Grandson Star in sequence after the Son Star; the Imperial Seat remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: " The court ordered the Great Heavenly Thearch and Northern Pole specially elevated to the first niche, the Grandson Star placed in sequence after the Son Star, and the Imperial Seat left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 欽若又言：「帝坐止三，紫微、太微者已列第二等，唯天市一坐在第三等。

translations.literal: Qinruo again stated: "Imperial Seats number only three; Purple Subtlety and Supreme Palace are already listed in the second rank — only the Heavenly Market seat is in the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo added: "There are only three Imperial Seats; Purple Subtlety and Supreme Palace are already in the second rank — only the Heavenly Market seat remains in the third.

sentences.zh: 按《晉志》，大角及心中星但雲天王坐，實與帝坐不類。

translations.literal: According to the Jin Treatise, Great Horn and the star at Heart only say Heavenly King Seat — in truth they are not of the same category as Imperial Seat.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Jin Treatise, Great Horn and the star at Heart are merely called Heavenly King Seats — they are not truly of the same category as the Imperial Seat.

sentences.zh: 」詔特升第二龕。

translations.literal: " An edict specially elevated it to the second niche.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered it specially elevated to the second niche.

sentences.zh: 舊郊丘，神位板皆有司題署，命欽若改造之。

translations.literal: At the old suburban mound and hill, spirit position tablets were all inscribed by the responsible officials; Qinruo was ordered to remake them.
translations.idiomatic: At the old suburban altar, spirit-seat tablets had all been inscribed by the responsible officials; Qinruo was ordered to remake them.

sentences.zh: 至是，欽若奉板便殿，壇上四位，塗以朱漆金字，余皆黑漆，第一等金字，第二等黃字，第三等以降朱字，悉貯漆匣，覆以黃縑帊。

translations.literal: At this time Qinruo presented the tablets in the side hall; the four positions on the altar were coated with cinnabar lacquer and gold characters; the rest were black lacquer — first rank gold characters, second rank yellow characters, third rank and below cinnabar characters — all stored in lacquer cases, covered with yellow silk cloth.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Qinruo presented the tablets in the side hall: the four seats on the altar were finished in cinnabar lacquer with gold characters; the rest in black lacquer — first rank in gold, second in yellow, third rank and below in cinnabar — all stored in lacquer cases covered with yellow silk cloth.

sentences.zh: 帝降階觀之，即付有司。

translations.literal: The emperor descended the steps to view them and immediately handed them to the responsible officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended the steps to inspect them and immediately entrusted them to the responsible officials.

sentences.zh: 又以新定《壇圖》，五帝、五嶽、中鎮、河漢合在第三等。

translations.literal: According to the newly fixed Altar Diagram, the Five Thearchs, Five Sacred Mountains, Central Marchmount, and River Han were combined in the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under the newly fixed Altar Diagram, the Five Thearchs, Five Sacred Mountains, Central Marchmount, and River Han were all placed in the third rank.

sentences.zh: 四年，判太常禮院孫奭言：「准禮，冬至祀圜丘，有司攝事，以天神六百九十位從祀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Ritual Office Sun Shi stated: "According to the rites, at the winter solstice sacrifice to the Round Mound, when officials perform the ceremony by proxy, six hundred ninety heavenly spirits attend in worship.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Sun Shi, acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Ritual Office, observed: "According to the rites, when officials perform the winter solstice sacrifice to the Round Mound by proxy, 690 heavenly spirits attend in worship.

sentences.zh: 今惟有五方上帝及五人神十七位，天皇大帝以下並不設位。

translations.literal: Now there are only the Five Directional Supreme Thearchs and seventeen human spirits — from the Great Heavenly Thearch downward no positions are established.
translations.idiomatic: At present only the Five Directional Supreme Thearchs and seventeen human spirits have seats; from the Great Heavenly Thearch downward, no positions are established at all.

sentences.zh: 且太昊、勾芒，惟孟夏雩祀、季秋大享及之，今乃祀於冬至，恐未協宜。

translations.literal: Moreover, Taihao and Goumang are reached only at the midsummer rain sacrifice and the autumn great offering — to sacrifice to them now at the winter solstice is feared not to be appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Taihao and Goumang are worshipped only at the midsummer rain sacrifice and the autumn great offering — to include them in the winter solstice rites is likely inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 」翰林學士晁迥等言：「按《開寶通禮》：圜丘，有司攝事，祀昊天、配帝、五方帝、日月、五星、中官、外官、眾星總六百八十七位；

translations.literal: " Hanlin Academician Chao Jiong and others stated: "According to the Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao: at the Round Mound, when officials perform by proxy, they sacrifice to Vast Heaven, the matching thearch, the Five Directional Thearchs, sun and moon, Five Stars, inner-palace, outer-palace, and host of stars — six hundred eighty-seven positions in all;
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Chao Jiong and others replied: "According to the Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao, when officials perform the Round Mound sacrifice by proxy, they worship Vast Heaven, the matching thearch, the Five Directional Thearchs, sun and moon, Five Stars, inner-palace, outer-palace, and host of stars — 687 positions in all;

sentences.zh: 雩祀、大享，昊天、配帝、五天帝、五人帝、五官總十七位；

translations.literal: at the rain sacrifice and great offering, Vast Heaven, matching thearch, Five Heavenly Thearchs, Five Human Thearchs, and Five Officials — seventeen positions in all;
translations.idiomatic: at the rain sacrifice and great offering, Vast Heaven, the matching thearch, the Five Heavenly Thearchs, Five Human Thearchs, and Five Officials — 17 positions in all;

sentences.zh: 方丘，祭皇地祇、配帝、神州、嶽鎮、海瀆七十一位。

translations.literal: at the Square Mound, sacrifice to Imperial Earth Spirit, matching thearch, Divine Land, marchmounts, and sea and river — seventy-one positions.
translations.idiomatic: at the Square Mound, Imperial Earth Spirit, the matching thearch, Divine Land, marchmounts, and sea and river — 71 positions.

sentences.zh: 今司天監所設圜丘、雩祀、明堂、方丘並七十位，即是方丘有嶽、瀆從祀，圜丘無星辰，而反以人帝從祀。

translations.literal: Now what the Directorate of Astronomy has established for Round Mound, rain sacrifice, Bright Hall, and Square Mound totals only seventy positions — that is, the Square Mound has mountains and rivers in attendant worship, while the Round Mound has no stars and yet human thearchs in attendant worship instead.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Astronomy now assigns only 70 positions each to the Round Mound, rain sacrifice, Bright Hall, and Square Mound — meaning the Square Mound includes mountains and rivers in attendant worship, while the Round Mound omits the stars and substitutes human thearchs instead.

sentences.zh: 望如奭請，以《通禮》及神位為定，其有增益者如後敕。

translations.literal: It is hoped that, as Sun Shi requested, the Comprehensive Rites and spirit positions be taken as fixed; any additions would follow later edicts.
translations.idiomatic: We request that, as Sun Shi proposed, the Comprehensive Rites and spirit positions be taken as the standard, with any additions to follow by subsequent edict.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，議禮局上《五禮新儀》：皇帝祀昊天上帝，太史設神位版，昊天上帝位於壇上北方南向，席以稿秸；

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe, the Deliberative Bureau on Rites presented the New Regulations for the Five Rites: when the emperor sacrifices to Vast Heaven Supreme Thearch, the Grand Astrologer sets out spirit position tablets — the Vast Heaven Supreme Thearch's position is on the altar in the north facing south, with a mat of straw;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenghe (1113), the Deliberative Bureau on Rites presented the New Regulations for the Five Rites: when the emperor sacrifices to Vast Heaven Supreme Thearch, the Grand Astrologer sets out spirit-seat tablets — Vast Heaven Supreme Thearch is placed on the altar in the north, facing south, on a mat of straw;

sentences.zh: 太祖位於壇上東方西向，席以蒲越；

translations.literal: Taizu is on the altar in the east facing west, with a mat of cattail;
translations.idiomatic: Taizu is placed on the altar in the east, facing west, on a cattail mat;

sentences.zh: 天皇大帝、五帝、大明、夜明、北極九位於第一龕；

translations.literal: the Great Heavenly Thearch, Five Thearchs, Great Brightness, Night Brightness, and Northern Pole — nine positions in the first niche;
translations.idiomatic: the Great Heavenly Thearch, Five Thearchs, Great Brightness, Night Brightness, and Northern Pole — nine seats in the first niche;

sentences.zh: 北斗、太一、帝坐、五帝內坐、五星、十二辰、河漢等內官神位五十有四於第二龕；

translations.literal: Northern Dipper, Supreme One, Imperial Seat, inner seats of the Five Thearchs, Five Stars, Twelve Chronograms, River Han, and other inner-palace spirit positions — fifty-four in the second niche;
translations.idiomatic: the Northern Dipper, Supreme One, Imperial Seat, inner seats of the Five Thearchs, Five Stars, Twelve Chronograms, River Han, and other inner-palace spirits — 54 seats in the second niche;

sentences.zh: 二十八宿等中官神位百五十有九於第三龕；

translations.literal: Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions and other central-palace spirit positions — one hundred fifty-nine in the third niche;
translations.idiomatic: the Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions and other central-palace spirits — 159 seats in the third niche;

sentences.zh: 外官神位一百有六於內壝之內；

translations.literal: outer-palace spirit positions — one hundred six within the inner enclosure;
translations.idiomatic: outer-palace spirits — 106 seats within the inner enclosure;

sentences.zh: 眾星三百有六十於內壝之外。

translations.literal: host of stars — three hundred sixty outside the inner enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: the host of stars — 360 seats beyond the inner enclosure.

sentences.zh: 第一龕席以稿秸，余以莞席，皆內向配位。

translations.literal: The first niche uses straw mats; the rest use sedge mats — all inward-facing matching positions.
translations.idiomatic: The first niche uses straw mats; the rest use sedge mats — all matching positions face inward.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，詔以四月幸西京，有事於南郊。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year, an edict ordered that in the fourth month the emperor would visit the Western Capital and perform affairs at the Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year, an edict announced that in the fourth month the emperor would visit the Western Capital to perform the Southern Suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 自國初以來，南郊四祭及感生帝、皇地祇、神州凡七祭，並以四祖迭配。

translations.literal: Since the founding of the state, the four sacrifices at the Southern Suburb together with the Life-Generating Thearch, Imperial Earth Spirit, and Divine Land — seven sacrifices in all — all used the four ancestors in rotation as matches.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the dynasty, the four Southern Suburban sacrifices together with the Life-Generating Thearch, Imperial Earth Spirit, and Divine Land — seven rites in all — had all employed the four ancestors in rotation as matching spirits.

sentences.zh: 太祖親郊者四，並以宣祖配。

translations.literal: Taizu personally performed suburban sacrifice four times, all with Xuandi as match.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu personally performed the suburban sacrifice four times, each time with Xuandi as the matching spirit.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，其七祭但以宣祖、太祖更配。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended the throne, for the seven sacrifices only Xuandi and Taizu were rotated as matches.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong ascended the throne, the seven sacrifices employed only Xuandi and Taizu in rotation as matching spirits.

sentences.zh: 是歲親享天地，始奉太祖升侑。

translations.literal: That year, when he personally enjoyed Heaven and Earth, he first presented Taizu to ascend as assistant.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when he personally worshipped Heaven and Earth, he first presented Taizu to ascend as the assisting spirit.

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年冬至親郊，從禮儀使扈蒙之議，復以宣祖配。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice personal suburban sacrifice in the first year of Yongxi, following Commissioner of Rites Hu Meng's proposal, Xuandi was again made match.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice suburban sacrifice in the first year of Yongxi (984), following Commissioner of Rites Hu Meng's proposal, Xuandi was again made the matching spirit.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，禮儀使蘇易簡言：「親祀圜丘，以宣祖配，此則符聖人大孝之道，成嚴父配天之儀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, Commissioner of Rites Su Yijian stated: "When personally sacrificing at the Round Mound, to match Xuandi accords with the sage's great filial way and completes the ceremony of the revered father matching Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year, Commissioner of Rites Su Yijian argued: "To match Xuandi at a personal sacrifice to the Round Mound accords with the sage's path of great filial piety and fulfills the ceremony of the revered father matching Heaven.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝光啟丕圖，恭臨大寶，以聖授聖，傳於無窮。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu brilliantly opened the great enterprise, reverently received the great treasure, the sage transmitting to the sage, passing on without end.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu brilliantly inaugurated the great enterprise and reverently received the throne, the sage transmitting sovereignty to the sage in an unending succession.

sentences.zh: 按唐永徽中，以高祖、太宗同配上帝。

translations.literal: According to Tang, in the Yonghui period, Gaozu and Taizong were jointly matched to the Supreme Thearch.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang, during the Yonghui period, Gaozu and Taizong were jointly matched to the Supreme Thearch.

sentences.zh: 欲望將來親祀郊丘，奉宣祖、太祖同配；

translations.literal: It is desired that in future personal sacrifices at the suburban mound and hill, Xuandi and Taizu be jointly presented as matches;
translations.idiomatic: We request that in future personal sacrifices at the suburban altar, Xuandi and Taizu be jointly presented as matching spirits;

sentences.zh: 其常祀祈穀、神州、明堂，以宣祖崇配；

translations.literal: for the regular sacrifices of praying for grain, Divine Land, and Bright Hall, Xuandi be honored as match;
translations.idiomatic: for the regular sacrifices of praying for grain, Divine Land, and the Bright Hall, Xuandi be honored as the matching spirit;

sentences.zh: 圜丘、北郊、雩祀，以太祖崇配。

translations.literal: for Round Mound, Northern Suburb, and rain sacrifice, Taizu be honored as match.
translations.idiomatic: and for the Round Mound, Northern Suburb, and rain sacrifice, Taizu be honored as the matching spirit.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 真宗至道三年十一月，有司言：「冬至圜丘、孟夏雩祀、夏至方丘，請奉太宗配；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Zhidao under Zhenzong, the responsible officials stated: "At winter solstice Round Mound, midsummer rain sacrifice, and summer solstice Square Mound, we request presenting Taizong as match;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year of Zhidao (997), the responsible officials proposed: "At the winter solstice Round Mound, midsummer rain sacrifice, and summer solstice Square Mound sacrifices, we request Taizong as the matching spirit;

sentences.zh: 上辛祈谷、季秋明堂，奉太祖配；

translations.literal: at upper xin praying for grain and autumn Bright Hall, present Taizu as match;
translations.idiomatic: at the upper xin day praying-for-grain sacrifice and the autumn Bright Hall sacrifice, Taizu as match;

sentences.zh: 上辛祀感生帝、孟冬祭神州地祇，奉宣祖配；

translations.literal: at upper xin sacrificing to the Life-Generating Thearch and mid-winter sacrificing to the Divine Land Earth Spirit, present Xuandi as match;
translations.idiomatic: at the upper xin sacrifice to the Life-Generating Thearch and the mid-winter sacrifice to the Divine Land Earth Spirit, Xuandi as match;

sentences.zh: 其親郊，奉太祖、太宗並配。

translations.literal: at personal suburban sacrifice, present Taizu and Taizong jointly as matches.
translations.idiomatic: and at personal suburban sacrifice, Taizu and Taizong jointly as matching spirits.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved by edict.

sentences.zh: 乾興元年，真宗崩，詔禮官定遷郊祀配帝，乃請：「祈穀及祭神州地祇，以太祖配；

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianxing, Zhenzong passed away; an edict ordered ritual officials to fix the matching thearchs for suburban sacrifice after the move of the capital, and they requested: "For praying for grain and sacrificing to the Divine Land Earth Spirit, Taizu as match;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianxing (1022), after Zhenzong's death, an edict ordered ritual officials to determine the matching spirits for suburban sacrifice following the capital's relocation; they proposed: "For the praying-for-grain and Divine Land Earth Spirit sacrifices, Taizu as match;

sentences.zh: 雩祀及昊天上帝及皇地祇，乙太宗配；

translations.literal: for rain sacrifice and Vast Heaven Supreme Thearch and Imperial Earth Spirit, on the day yi Taizong as match;
translations.idiomatic: for the rain sacrifice and for Vast Heaven Supreme Thearch and Imperial Earth Spirit, Taizong as match;

sentences.zh: 感生帝，以宣祖配；

translations.literal: for the Life-Generating Thearch, Xuandi as match;
translations.idiomatic: for the Life-Generating Thearch, Xuandi as match;

sentences.zh: 明堂，以真宗配；

translations.literal: for the Bright Hall, Zhenzong as match;
translations.idiomatic: for the Bright Hall, Zhenzong as match;

sentences.zh: 親祀郊丘，以太祖、太宗配。

translations.literal: for personal sacrifice at suburban mound and hill, Taizu and Taizong as matches.
translations.idiomatic: for personal suburban sacrifice, Taizu and Taizong as matching spirits.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 景祐二年郊，詔以太祖、太宗、真宗三廟萬世不遷。

translations.literal: At the suburban sacrifice in the second year of Jingyou, an edict declared that the temples of Taizu, Taizong, and Zhenzong would never be moved for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban sacrifice in the second year of Jingyou (1035), an edict declared that the temples of Taizu, Taizong, and Zhenzong would remain permanently enshrined for all generations.

sentences.zh: 南郊以太祖定配，二宗迭配，親祀皆侑。

translations.literal: At the Southern Suburb, Taizu was the fixed match; the two [later] ancestors rotated as matches; at personal sacrifice all were presented as assistants.
translations.idiomatic: At the Southern Suburb, Taizu was the fixed matching spirit, the two later emperors rotated as secondary matches, and at personal sacrifice all were presented as assisting spirits.

sentences.zh: 常祀圜丘、皇地祇配以太祖，祈谷、雩祀、神州配乙太宗，感生帝、明堂以宣祖、真宗配如舊。

translations.literal: At regular sacrifice, Round Mound and Imperial Earth Spirit matched with Taizu; praying for grain, rain sacrifice, and Divine Land matched on day yi with Taizong; Life-Generating Thearch and Bright Hall matched with Xuandi and Zhenzong as before.
translations.idiomatic: At regular sacrifice, the Round Mound and Imperial Earth Spirit were matched with Taizu; the praying-for-grain, rain, and Divine Land sacrifices with Taizong; the Life-Generating Thearch and Bright Hall with Xuandi and Zhenzong as before.

sentences.zh: 慶曆元年，判太常寺呂公綽言：「歷代郊祀，配位無側向，真宗示輔臣《封禪圖》曰：'嘗見郊祀昊天上帝，不以正坐，蓋皇地祇次之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingli, acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Lü Gongchuo stated: "Through the ages at suburban sacrifice, matching positions had no lateral orientation. Zhenzong showed his ministers the Diagram of Feng and Shan, saying: 'I once saw that at suburban sacrifice to Vast Heaven Supreme Thearch, He does not sit facing directly forward — for Imperial Earth Spirit is second.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qingli (1041), Lü Gongchuo, acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, observed: "Through the ages, suburban sacrifice matching positions had no fixed lateral orientation. Zhenzong once showed his ministers the Diagram of Feng and Shan, saying: "I once observed that at suburban sacrifice to Vast Heaven Supreme Thearch, He does not sit facing directly forward — for Imperial Earth Spirit ranks second.

sentences.zh: 今修登封，上帝宜當子位，太祖、太宗配位，宜比郊祀而斜置之。

translations.literal: Now in repairing the ascent of Feng, the Supreme Thearch should occupy the zi position; the matching positions of Taizu and Taizong should be compared to suburban sacrifice and placed obliquely.
translations.idiomatic: In performing the Feng ascent, the Supreme Thearch should occupy the zi position; the matching positions of Taizu and Taizong should follow suburban sacrifice practice and be placed obliquely.

sentences.zh: '其後，有司不諭先帝以告成報功、酌宜從變之意，每郊儀範，既引祥符側置之文，又載西向北上之禮，臨時擇一，未嘗考定。

translations.literal: ' Thereafter the responsible officials did not understand the former emperor's intent to report accomplishment and repay merit, to weigh what was fitting and follow change; at each suburban ritual manual they both cited the Xiangfu text on oblique placement and recorded the rite of facing west and proceeding north — choosing one at the moment, never examined and fixed.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter the responsible officials failed to grasp the former emperor's intent to report accomplishment and repay merit by adapting ritual as circumstances required; at each suburban sacrifice the ritual manuals cited both the Xiangfu text on oblique placement and the rite of facing west and proceeding north — choosing one provisionally without ever settling the matter.

sentences.zh: 」乃詔南郊祖宗之配，並以東方西向為定。

translations.literal: " An edict then fixed that for Southern Suburb matching of ancestors, all were to face west from the east.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict then fixed that at the Southern Suburb, all ancestral matching positions were to face west from the east.

sentences.zh: 皇祐五年郊，詔自今圜丘，三聖並侑。

translations.literal: At the suburban sacrifice in the fifth year of Huangyou, an edict ordered that from now on at the Round Mound, the three sage emperors all be presented as assistants.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban sacrifice in the fifth year of Huangyou (1053), an edict ordered that henceforth at the Round Mound all three sage emperors be presented as assisting spirits.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐六年，諫官楊畋論水災繇郊廟未順。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiayou, remonstrance official Yang Tian discussed flood disasters arising from suburban temples not being in accord.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiayou (1061), remonstrance official Yang Tian argued that the floods arose because suburban and temple rites were not properly ordered.

sentences.zh: 禮院亦言：「對越天地，神無二主。

translations.literal: The Ritual Office also stated: "In facing and responding to Heaven and Earth, spirits have no dual lords.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Office also observed: "In worshipping Heaven and Earth, there can be no dual sovereign among the spirits.

sentences.zh: 唐始用三祖同配，後遂罷之。

translations.literal: Tang first used three ancestors jointly matched, then later abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang first employed three ancestors as joint matches, then later abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 皇祐初，詔三聖並侑，後復迭配，未幾復並侑，以為定制。

translations.literal: Early in Huangyou, an edict ordered the three sage emperors all presented as assistants; later they again rotated as matches; before long all were again presented as assistants — taken as fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangyou, an edict ordered all three sage emperors presented as assistants; later they reverted to rotation; before long all three were again presented together — and this became the fixed regulation.

sentences.zh: 雖出孝思，然頗違經典，當時有司失於講求。

translations.literal: Although arising from filial thought, it rather violated the classics; the responsible officials of that time failed in investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Although motivated by filial devotion, it rather violated classical precedent; the responsible officials of that time had failed to investigate properly.

sentences.zh: 」下兩制議，翰林學士王珪等曰：「推尊以享帝，義之至也。

translations.literal: " The matter was sent down for deliberation by the two academies; Hanlin Academician Wang Gui and others stated: "Promoting the revered to enjoy the Thearch is the utmost of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: " The matter was referred to the two academies for deliberation; Hanlin Academician Wang Gui and others argued: "To honor the revered by sharing worship with the Thearch is the highest expression of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 然尊尊不可以瀆，故郊無二主。

translations.literal: Yet the exalted cannot be profaned; therefore at the suburb there is no dual lord.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the exalted must not be profaned; therefore at the suburban sacrifice there can be no dual sovereign.

sentences.zh: 今三後並侑，欲以致孝也，而適所以瀆乎享帝，非無以寧神也，請如禮官議。

translations.literal: Now with the three empresses all presented as assistants, intending to achieve filial piety, one thereby precisely profanes worship of the Thearch — this is not without means to pacify the spirits; we request following the Ritual Office's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: To present all three emperors as assistants, intending filial piety, in fact profanes the worship of the Thearch and fails to properly appease the spirits; we request following the Ritual Office's proposal.

sentences.zh: 」七年正月，詔南郊以太祖定配。

translations.literal: " In the first month of the seventh year, an edict ordered that at the Southern Suburb Taizu be the fixed match.
translations.idiomatic: " In the first month of the seventh year, an edict ordered that at the Southern Suburb Taizu be the fixed matching spirit.

sentences.zh: 高宗建炎二年，車駕至揚州，築壇于江都縣之東南。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan under Gaozong, the imperial carriage reached Yangzhou and an altar was built southeast of Jiangdu County.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyan (1128), Emperor Gaozong reached Yangzhou and an altar was built southeast of Jiangdu County.

sentences.zh: 是歲冬至，祀昊天上帝，以太祖配。

translations.literal: That year at the winter solstice, Vast Heaven Supreme Thearch was sacrificed to, with Taizu as match.
translations.idiomatic: That winter solstice, the court sacrificed to Vast Heaven Supreme Thearch with Taizu as the matching spirit.

sentences.zh: 度宗鹹淳二年，將舉郊祀，時復議以高宗參配。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianchun under Duzong, when suburban sacrifice was about to be performed, at the time it was again debated whether Gaozong should participate as match.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianchun (1266), as suburban sacrifice was about to be performed, the court again debated whether Gaozong should participate as a matching spirit.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎兼中書門下省檢正洪燾等議，以為：「物無二本，事無二初，舜之郊嚳，商之郊契，周郊後稷，皆所以推原其始也。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrent Secretariat-Chancellery Reviewer Hong Tao and others deliberated, holding that: "Things have no dual roots, affairs no dual beginnings — Shun's suburban sacrifice to Ku, Shang's suburban sacrifice to Qi, Zhou's suburban sacrifice to Hou Ji all trace back to their origins.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrent Secretariat-Chancellery Reviewer Hong Tao and others argued: "Things have no dual roots and affairs no dual beginnings — Shun's suburban sacrifice to Ku, the Shang's to Qi, and the Zhou's to Hou Ji all trace worship back to its origin.

sentences.zh: 禮者，所以別等差，視儀則，遠而尊者配於郊，近而親者配於明堂，明有等也。

translations.literal: Rites are what distinguish ranks and degrees, observe ceremonial norms — the distant and exalted are matched at the suburb, the near and intimate at the Bright Hall; clearly there are ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Rites exist to distinguish ranks and observe ceremonial norms: the distant and exalted are matched at the suburb, the near and intimate at the Bright Hall — clearly there are distinctions of rank.

sentences.zh: 臣等謂宜如紹興故事，奉太宗配，將來明堂遵用先皇帝彝典，以高宗參侑，庶於報本之禮、奉先之孝，為兩盡其至。

translations.literal: We your subjects hold it fitting to follow the Shaoxing precedent, presenting Taizong as match; when the Bright Hall comes, to follow the former emperor's constant regulations with Gaozong participating as assistant — thus in the rites of repaying the root and the filial piety of honoring ancestors, both may reach their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: We hold that the court should follow the Shaoxing precedent, presenting Taizong as match; at the future Bright Hall sacrifice, follow the former emperor's established regulations with Gaozong as assisting spirit — thus fulfilling both the rite of repaying the root and the filial piety of honoring ancestors to the fullest.

sentences.zh: 」詔恭依。

translations.literal: " An edict respectfully approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The court respectfully approved.

sentences.zh: 儀注。

translations.literal: Ritual Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual Protocol.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年八月，禮儀使陶穀言：「饗廟、郊天，兩日行禮，從祀官前七日皆合於尚書省受誓戒，自來一日之內受兩處誓戒，有虧虔潔。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Qiande, Commissioner of Rites Tao Gu stated: "Enjoying the temple and sacrificing to Heaven at the suburb — the rites performed on two days — attendant sacrifice officials seven days beforehand should all receive oath-abstention at the Secretariat; from old, receiving oath-abstention at two places within one day impairs reverent purity.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Qiande (963), Commissioner of Rites Tao Gu observed: "When temple worship and suburban sacrifice to Heaven are performed on consecutive days, attendant officials should receive oath-abstention at the Secretariat seven days in advance; receiving oath-abstention at two places on the same day, as had been done, impairs reverent purity.

sentences.zh: 今擬十一月十六日行郊禮，望依禮文於八日先受從享太廟誓戒，九日別受郊天誓戒，其日請放朝參。

translations.literal: Now planning to perform suburban rites on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month, it is hoped that according to ritual texts, on the eighth day they first receive oath-abstention for attending enjoyment at the Imperial Temple, on the ninth day separately receive oath-abstention for suburban Heaven, and on those days court attendance be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: With suburban rites planned for the sixteenth day of the eleventh month, we request that on the eighth day officials first receive oath-abstention for attending at the Imperial Temple, on the ninth day separately receive oath-abstention for suburban Heaven, and that court attendance be suspended on those days.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 自後百官受誓戒於朝堂，宗室受於太廟。

translations.literal: Thereafter all officials received oath-abstention in the court hall; the imperial clan received it at the Imperial Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter all officials received oath-abstention in the court hall, and the imperial clan at the Imperial Temple.

sentences.zh: 祭之日均用丑時，秋夏以一刻，春冬以七刻，前二日遣官奏告。

translations.literal: On the day of sacrifice all used the chou hour; in autumn and summer one quarter, in spring and winter seven quarters; two days beforehand officials were dispatched to report.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices were all performed at the chou hour — one quarter after midnight in autumn and summer, seven quarters in spring and winter — with officials dispatched to report two days beforehand.

sentences.zh: 配帝之室，儀鸞司設大次、小次及文武侍臣、蕃客之次，太常設樂位、神位、版位等事。

translations.literal: In the chamber of the matching thearch, the Imperial Insignia Office set up the great tent, small tent, and tents for civil and military attendant ministers and foreign guests; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set up music positions, spirit positions, tablet positions, and related matters.
translations.idiomatic: In the chamber of the matching spirit, the Imperial Insignia Office erected the great and small tents and quarters for civil and military attendants and foreign guests; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices arranged music stands, spirit seats, tablet positions, and related matters.

sentences.zh: 前一日司尊彝帥其屬以法陳祭器於堂東，僕射、禮部尚書視滌濯告潔，禮部尚書、侍郎省牲，光祿卿奉牲，告充、告備，禮部尚書視鼎鑊，禮部侍郎視腥熟之節。

translations.literal: On the previous day the Director of Ritual Vessels led his subordinates to arrange sacrificial vessels by regulation east of the hall; the Grand Tutor and Minister of Rites inspected washing and announced purity; Minister and Vice Minister of Rites inspected the sacrificial animals; the Minister of Imperial Household presented the animals, announcing sufficiency and readiness; the Minister of Rites inspected the cauldrons; the Vice Minister of Rites inspected the stages of raw and cooked.
translations.idiomatic: On the previous day the Director of Ritual Vessels led his staff to arrange sacrificial vessels east of the hall according to regulation; the Grand Tutor and Minister of Rites inspected the washing and announced purity; the Minister and Vice Minister of Rites inspected the sacrificial animals; the Minister of Imperial Household presented them, announcing sufficiency and readiness; the Minister of Rites inspected the cauldrons and the Vice Minister the stages of raw and cooked meat.

sentences.zh: 祭之旦，光祿卿率其屬取籩、豆、簠、簋實之。

translations.literal: At dawn of the sacrifice, the Minister of Imperial Household led his subordinates to take the baskets, cups, grain vessels, and food vessels and fill them.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the day of sacrifice, the Minister of Imperial Household led his staff to fill the baskets, cups, grain vessels, and food vessels.

sentences.zh: 及薦腥，禮部尚書帥其屬薦籩、豆、簠、簋，戶部、兵部、工部尚書薦三牲之腥熟俎。

translations.literal: When presenting raw meat, the Minister of Rites led his subordinates to present baskets, cups, grain vessels, and food vessels; the Ministers of Revenue, War, and Works presented the raw and cooked trays of the three sacrificial animals.
translations.idiomatic: When presenting the raw offerings, the Minister of Rites led his staff to present the baskets, cups, grain vessels, and food vessels; the Ministers of Revenue, War, and Works presented the raw and cooked trays of the three sacrificial animals.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，各徹，而有司受之以出。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, each was withdrawn, and the responsible officials received them to take out.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were complete, each offering was withdrawn and received by the responsible officials to be removed.

sentences.zh: 晡後，郊社令帥其屬掃除，御史按視之。

translations.literal: After the afternoon, the Director of Suburban and Altar Affairs led his subordinates to sweep clean; the censor inspected.
translations.idiomatic: In the afternoon, the Director of Suburban and Altar Affairs led his staff in sweeping the site clean, and the censor inspected.

sentences.zh: 奏中嚴外辦以禮部侍郎，請解嚴以禮部郎中。

translations.literal: To announce inner vigilance and outer readiness, the Vice Minister of Rites; to request release of vigilance, the Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Minister of Rites announced inner vigilance and outer readiness; the Director of the Ministry of Rites requested release of vigilance.

sentences.zh: 贊者設亞、終獻位於小次之南，宗室位於其後；

translations.literal: The invoker set the secondary and final offering positions south of the small tent, with the imperial clan behind them;
translations.idiomatic: The invoker placed the secondary and final offering positions south of the small tent, with the imperial clan behind them;

sentences.zh: 設公卿位於亞、終獻之南，分獻官位於公卿之後，執事者又在其後，俱重行，西向北上。

translations.literal: set duke and minister positions south of the secondary and final offerings, separate offering officials behind the dukes and ministers, executants again behind them — all in double rows, facing west and proceeding north.
translations.idiomatic: placed the dukes and ministers south of the secondary and final offerings, separate offering officials behind them, and executants behind those — all in double rows, facing west and proceeding north.

sentences.zh: 其致福也，太牢以牛左肩、臂、臑折九個，少牢以羊左肩七個、犆豕以左肩五個。

translations.literal: In presenting blessings, the great offering used nine pieces from the ox's left shoulder, arm, and shank; the lesser offering seven pieces from the sheep's left shoulder; the single pig five pieces from the left shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: In presenting blessings, the great offering comprised nine pieces from the ox's left shoulder, arm, and shank; the lesser offering seven pieces from the sheep's left shoulder; and the single pig five pieces from the left shoulder.

sentences.zh: 有司攝事、進胙皆如禮。

translations.literal: When officials performed by proxy and presented the sacrificial meat, all followed the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When officials performed the ceremony by proxy and presented the sacrificial meat, all followed established ritual.

sentences.zh: 太尉展視以授使者，再拜稽首。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant displayed and inspected, then handed to the envoy, who bowed twice and touched his forehead to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant displayed and inspected the offering, then handed it to the envoy, who bowed twice and touched his forehead to the ground.

sentences.zh: 既享，大宴，號曰飲福，自宰臣而下至應執事及樂工、馭車馬人等，並均給有差，以為定式。

translations.literal: After the enjoyment, a great feast was held, called Drinking Blessings; from the chief minister down to those who should execute affairs, musicians, chariot and horse handlers, and others — all were equally distributed with differences, established as fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: After the sacrifice, a great feast called Drinking Blessings was held; from the chief minister down to executants, musicians, and charioteers — all received shares in graded amounts, established as fixed regulation.

sentences.zh: 是歲十一月日至，皇帝服袞冕，執圭，合祭天地於圜丘，還禦明德門樓，肆赦。

translations.literal: That year on the day of the eleventh month's solstice, the emperor wore dark robes and cap, held the scepter, jointly sacrificed to Heaven and Earth at the Round Mound, returned to ascend the Mingde Gate tower, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: That year on the winter solstice of the eleventh month, the emperor wore dark robes and cap, held the scepter, jointly sacrificed to Heaven and Earth at the Round Mound, returned to ascend the Mingde Gate tower, and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖二年，詔加真宗諡，上謂輔臣曰：「郊祀重事，朕欲就禁中習儀，其令禮官草具以聞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiansheng under Renzong, an edict added Zhenzong's posthumous title; the emperor told his ministers: "Suburban sacrifice is a weighty affair; I wish to practice the rites within the Forbidden City — have the ritual officials draft the arrangements and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiansheng (1024), an edict added Zhenzong's posthumous title; the emperor told his ministers: "Suburban sacrifice is a weighty affair; I wish to rehearse the rites within the Forbidden City — have the ritual officials draft the arrangements and report.

sentences.zh: 」先郊三日，奉諡冊寶於太廟。

translations.literal: " Three days before the suburban sacrifice, the posthumous title tablets and seals were presented at the Imperial Temple.
translations.idiomatic: " Three days before the suburban sacrifice, the posthumous title tablets and seals were presented at the Imperial Temple.

sentences.zh: 次日，薦享玉清昭應、景靈宮，宿太廟。

translations.literal: The next day, offerings were presented at Yujing Zhaoying and Jingling Palaces; he lodged at the Imperial Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, offerings were presented at the Yujing Zhaoying and Jingling Palaces, and the emperor lodged at the Imperial Temple.

sentences.zh: 既享，赴青城，至大次，就更衣壇改服袞冕行事。

translations.literal: After the enjoyment, he proceeded to the Green City, reached the great tent, then at the dressing altar changed into dark robes and cap to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: After the temple worship, he proceeded to the Green City, reached the great tent, and at the dressing altar changed into dark robes and cap to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 五年，郊後擇日恭謝，大禮使王曾請節廟樂，帝曰：「三年一享，不敢憚勞也。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, after the suburban sacrifice a day was chosen for reverent thanksgiving; the Grand Ritual Commissioner Wang Zeng requested reducing temple music; the emperor said: "Once every three years we enjoy — I dare not shrink from the labor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, after the suburban sacrifice a day was chosen for reverent thanksgiving; Grand Ritual Commissioner Wang Zeng requested reducing the temple music; the emperor replied: "We worship the temple only once every three years — I dare not shrink from the effort.

sentences.zh: 」三獻終，增禮生七人，各引本室太祝升殿，徹豆。

translations.literal: " When the three offerings were complete, seven additional ritual students were added; each led the chief invoker of his chamber up the hall to withdraw the beans.
translations.idiomatic: " When the three offerings were complete, seven additional ritual students were added; each led the chief invoker of his chamber up the hall to withdraw the offerings.

sentences.zh: 三日，又齋長春殿，謝玉清昭應宮。

translations.literal: On the third day, he again fasted at the Changchun Hall and gave thanks at the Yujing Zhaoying Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day, he again fasted at the Changchun Hall and gave thanks at the Yujing Zhaoying Palace.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，賀皇太后，比籍田，勞酒儀，略如元會。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, he congratulated the Empress Dowager; compared to the ceremonial plowing, the protocol of toasting with labor wine was roughly like the New Year's audience.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were complete, he congratulated the Empress Dowager; the protocol of toasting with labor wine resembled that of the New Year's audience, much like the ceremonial plowing ceremony.

sentences.zh: 其恭謝云：「臣某虔遵舊典，郊祀禮成，中外協心，不勝歡抃。

translations.literal: The reverent thanksgiving stated: "Your subject so-and-so reverently follows the old regulations; the suburban sacrifice rites are complete; within and without are of one heart — unable to contain our joy.
translations.idiomatic: The reverent thanksgiving read: "Your subject reverently follows the established regulations; the suburban sacrifice rites are complete; within and without the court are united in joy beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 」宣答曰：「皇帝德備孝恭，禮成嚴配，萬國稱頌，歡豫增深。

translations.literal: " The response announced: "The emperor's virtue is complete in filial reverence; the rites are accomplished in solemn matching; the ten thousand states praise — joy and delight increase deeply.
translations.idiomatic: " The response announced: "The emperor's virtue is complete in filial reverence; the rites are accomplished in solemn matching; the myriad states offer praise — our joy and delight deepen.

sentences.zh: 」帝再拜還內。

translations.literal: " The emperor bowed twice and returned within.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor bowed twice and returned within.

sentences.zh: 樞密使以下稱賀，閣門使宣答，樞密副使升殿侍立，百官稱賀。

translations.literal: From the Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner down, congratulations were offered; the Gatekeeper Commissioner announced the response; the Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs ascended the hall to attend standing; all officials offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: From the Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner down, congratulations were offered; the Gatekeeper Commissioner announced the response; the Vice Commissioner ascended the hall to attend; and all officials offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 酒三行，還內殿，受命婦賀，司賓自殿側幕次引內命婦於殿庭，北向立，尚儀奏：「請皇太后即御坐。

translations.literal: After three rounds of wine, he returned to the inner hall; appointed consorts offered congratulations; the Master of Guests from the side curtain of the hall led the inner appointed consorts into the court, standing facing north; the Director of Ceremonies reported: "We request the Empress Dowager to take her throne.
translations.idiomatic: After three rounds of wine, he returned to the inner hall for congratulations from appointed consorts; the Master of Guests led the inner appointed consorts from the side curtain into the court to stand facing north; the Director of Ceremonies reported: "We request the Empress Dowager to take her throne.

sentences.zh: 」司賓贊：「再拜。

translations.literal: " The Master of Guests intoned: "Bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: " The Master of Guests intoned: "Bow twice.

sentences.zh: 」引班首升自西階，稱封號妾某氏等言：「郊祀再舉，福祚鹹均，凡在照臨，不勝忻抃。

translations.literal: " He led the head of the rank up the west steps; they stated their titles and names, saying: "The suburban sacrifice has been performed again; blessings and fortune are equally shared; all within your illumination — unable to contain our joy.
translations.idiomatic: " He led the senior consort up the west steps; bearing their titles they said: "The suburban sacrifice has been performed again; blessings and fortune are equally shared; all within your illumination rejoice beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 」降，再拜。

translations.literal: " They descended and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " They descended and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 尚宮承旨，降自東階，稱「皇太后聖旨」，又再拜。

translations.literal: The Palace Director received the edict, descended the east steps, announced "By the sacred edict of the Empress Dowager," and they bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Director received the edict, descended the east steps, announced "By the sacred edict of the Empress Dowager," and they bowed twice again.

sentences.zh: 司賓宣答曰「已成钜禮，歡豫良深。

translations.literal: The Master of Guests announced the response: "The great rites are accomplished; joy and delight are truly deep.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Guests announced the response: "The great rites are accomplished; our joy and delight are profound.

sentences.zh: 」皆再拜。

translations.literal: " All bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " All bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 次外命婦賀，如內命婦儀，退，皆赴別殿賀皇帝，惟不致詞，不宣答。

translations.literal: Next the outer appointed consorts offered congratulations, following the inner consorts' protocol; they withdrew and all proceeded to a separate hall to congratulate the emperor — only without presenting speeches or announcing responses.
translations.idiomatic: Next the outer appointed consorts offered congratulations following the same protocol; they withdrew and all proceeded to a separate hall to congratulate the emperor — only without formal speeches or announced responses.
